newsitem.title: UK: Copper grabs $2,600, but LME pace slow.
newsitem.headline: Copper grabs $2,600, but LME pace slow.

text.p: Copper prices caught hold of the $2,600 a tonne level during early Tuesday LME pre-market trading, but conditions were slow.
The copper market was maintaining the upward momentum of late Monday, with some light speculative buying lifting prices to $2,602 a tonne, up $14 from the afternoon kerb close.
A 1,550-tonne stock fall was supportive, although there was a rise overnight in Comex inventories, which tended to offset this.
In the short-term the market is overbought, so the current modest advance may stall prior to testing the 13-month high of $2,609 and the resistance overhead.
"Everybody knows that the market has got itself overbought, so it is a bit of a stand-off," one trader said.
Aluminium prices also moved higher, partly in response to the copper market trend, but with the added impetus of another 4,350-tonne stock decline.
"There was a bit of mixed buying - nothing in particular though," the trader said.

Three months prices edged up to $1,590 a tonne, a gain of $8 from the previous kerb. Charts are bearish, however, with the market more likely to test $1,575 as opposed to $1,600 in the short-term, technicians said.
Activity in the rest of the complex was thin, with little significant movement seen.
Zinc edged up after a modest 25-tonne inventory increase put on hold concerns over sizeable Chinese deliveries into Singapore. The market was $3 higher at $1,376.
Lead was little changed at $622, consolidating after Monday's liquidation from above $630.
Nickel was unchanged at $7,250, tin was indicated at $5,530/50, and alloy was quoted at $1,470/78. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
